headline: Taylor, Texas, has unanimously approved a deal to bring a 660-acre data centre and gas power plant campus into the city despite months of resident opposition.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered to 5: the vote was on Thu 8 Oct 2026, before the 9 Oct start of the window; the report was read in full and nothing is overstated.
importance_line: Residents of Taylor, a city of about 18,400, face a very large campus with its own gas plant, and the city says annexation gives it more control, but the jobs and tax figures are the developers' estimates and opposition to data centres is spreading across Texas.
summary: The Austin American-Statesman reports that the Taylor City Council voted unanimously on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 for an agreement with Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers on a campus of 500 megawatts, with room for 500 more, powered by its own gas plant instead of the grid, with a one-time fill of reclaimed water for cooling, set distances from homes, the right for the city to suspend the project if rules are broken, at least $28.2 million for the community and no tax breaks. Most speakers at the meeting opposed it and asked for a pause until the state finishes the review of data centres that Governor Greg Abbott ordered, while city officials said an agreement was the only way to set design standards.
notes: Event date 8 Oct 2026 (before the window), reported 9 Oct. Texas context (Abbott's September order halting TCEQ permits) is from the article.
